links.title: Shoshan-Barmatz — VDAC1 in apoptosis & disease
links.desc: Varda Shoshan-Barmatz wrote the canonical review series on VDAC1 as a hub for metabolism, calcium and cell death. Any of them is a great foundation.

links.title: VDAC1 oligomerization & the apoptosis pore
links.desc: The mechanistic heart of the disease story: how VDAC1 grouping up forms a big pore that leaks mitochondrial contents.

links.title: VDAC1 in neurodegeneration & Alzheimer's
links.desc: Where my head lives — VDAC1's links to amyloid, tau and mitochondrial dysfunction in the brain.

links.title: ★ Kim et al., Science 2019 — VDAC oligomers, mtDNA release & lupus (the one)
links.desc: If you read a single VDAC1 paper, read this one. Kim, Shoshan-Barmatz and colleagues showed VDAC1 oligomers form the outer-membrane pore that releases mtDNA fragments and drives the interferon response — and that VBIT-4 blocks it and eases lupus in mice. It's the anchor of my whole VBIT reading list. (Science 366:1531–1536; PMID 31857488.)

links.title: VBIT-4 across disease models
links.desc: Follow-on work testing VDAC1-oligomerization inhibitors in metabolic, kidney, heart and brain models. See how far the idea reaches.

links.title: mtDNA → cGAS–STING → inflammation
links.desc: The immune side: why mitochondrial DNA in the wrong place acts like a danger signal. Context for why a leaky pore matters.
